content.title: Who Are the Key Players in a Fannie, Freddie IPO?
content.summary: The U.S. Treasury: A deal would likely involve the Treasury selling a portion of the stake it took in the firms in the 2008-09 financial crisis.  When the government put the firms under conservatorship, it wanted to ensure taxpayers—via the Treasury—were adequately repaid for the risk they took to stabilize the mortgage market.  Junior preferred shareholders: Below the senior preferred shares sit roughly $35 billion in outstanding junior preferred shares, according to a 2024 Congressional Budget Office report.
